strengths: The paper poses a clear, well-motivated research question (whether BEV representations are more effective than perspective-view image tokens for LLM spatial reasoning in driving) and conducts a systematic empirical study to answer it, which is a useful and underexplored comparison.

The representation study spans multiple LLM backbones (InternVL3-1B/8B, DeepSeek-VL) and two datasets (DriveLM-nuScenes, Ego3D) with several carefully constructed baselines (majority class, linear probe, task-specific detector), lending some credibility to the claim that BEV tokens can be aligned with language space nearly as well as a dedicated detection decoder.

The semantic distillation idea (using a frozen LLM as a supervisory signal via VQA to enrich a geometrically-trained BEV encoder while jointly retaining detection supervision) is a reasonable and relatively novel way to inject semantic/commonsense knowledge into structured perception representations.

Evaluation includes both open-loop (nuScenes L2) and, more importantly, closed-loop safety-critical evaluation (NeuroNCAP), which is more informative than the open-loop-only evaluations common in this literature.

The paper includes informative ablations (BEV downsampling strategy, VQA data-type ablation for distillation) and an honest discussion of a failure case, plus fairly detailed supplementary material aiding reproducibility (dataset splits, filtering criteria, training hyperparameters, license disclosures).
weaknesses: Generalizability is limited: all main experiments use a single BEV encoder/architecture (BEVFormer/UniAD) and a single VQA distillation dataset (DriveLM-nuScenes); the paper acknowledges this but attributes it entirely to compute cost, leaving open whether the core claims (BEV superiority, distillation benefit) transfer to other BEV architectures or richer VQA corpora.

Several evaluation sets are very small, undermining statistical confidence in some headline numbers: e.g., the Ego3D cross-view reasoning test split used for the widely advertised '46% accuracy improvement' contains only 162 questions total, with individual sub-categories as small as 34–43 samples.

The closed-loop NeuroNCAP improvement is nuanced: the 1B-distilled model's collision rate is essentially unchanged (0.63 vs. 0.62 baseline), and only the 8B model reduces collision rate (0.55); the improvement in NeuroNCAP score is driven mainly by reduced impact velocity rather than collision avoidance itself, which is a more modest safety benefit than the abstract's framing ('29% improvement in safety-critical scenarios') might suggest to a casual reader.

The 'Intuitive Interpretation: BEV as a Semantic Manifold' section introduces formal notation (a manifold M_teacher, an ideal embedding v*, Eq. 1) that is never made operational or verified—v* is stated to be inaccessible and the loss is only a qualitative 'approximation' via cross-entropy; this reads as post-hoc theoretical framing rather than a rigorous or falsifiable formalism, and does not add real technical content beyond the already-clear intuitive description.

The distillation ablation does not include a variant without the auxiliary detection loss, so the claim that joint detection training 'prevents catastrophic forgetting of spatial relationships' is asserted but not empirically verified.

The argument that BEV's advantage over I_ViT is not merely due to encoder capacity (Sec. 3.2) rests on comparing an object detection module of 'only 10% of the backbone size' and comparable accuracy despite 10x parameter difference, but this comparison confounds multiple factors (pretraining data/objective, architecture, task alignment) beyond parameter count, weakening the causal claim that gains stem purely from BEV's representational properties.

There is no baseline comparing BEVLM's LLM-distillation approach against a simpler alternative semantic-enrichment method (e.g., directly fusing VLM/CLIP features into the BEV grid or using auxiliary captioning losses without an LLM), which would help isolate whether the specific mechanism of LLM-based distillation is necessary versus any generic semantic auxiliary supervision.
